tasks.prompt: Water loss audit leadership case 10: real losses in the Hillcrest pressure district of an Ontario utility climb for three years even though reported main breaks fall, and the audit team must find the driver before setting the loss strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario system audit with supplied volume, billed volume, break records, district night flows and pressure records available.

evidence.label: Supplied volume for Hillcrest rose 9 percent over three years while billed authorized consumption stayed flat.
Reported main breaks in the district fell from 47 to 39 per year over the same period.
Average district pressure was raised from 450 to 530 kPa two years ago to serve a new high area and was never readjusted.
Night flow analysis shows background leakage up across the whole district, not concentrated at break sites.
A trial lowering one subdistrict back to 480 kPa cuts its night flow by 27 percent with no service complaints.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Customers in the district are stealing more water each year
The treatment plant supply meter has drifted high over three years
Fire hydrants are being left open across the district
Higher average pressure is driving up background leakage through many small joints and fittings, even as large breaks decline

inference.explanation: Background leakage rising everywhere, a pressure increase that precedes the loss rise, and a large night flow cut when pressure is lowered in a trial all point to pressure driven leakage. Theft or open hydrants would localize, and meter drift would not respond to a pressure trial.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation and guides the strategy?

options.label: Launch a customer theft investigation across the district
Develop a pressure management plan that gives the high area its own zone so general district pressure can return to proven levels
Accept the higher losses as the unavoidable cost of growth

nextClue.explanation: Zoning the high area tests whether general pressure can fall without harming high customers, which is the fix the trial supports.

clueText.nc-a: Losses are spread as background leakage, not concentrated theft, and the pressure trial already identified the driver.
clueText.nc-b: With the high area on its own zone, district night flow falls by 25 percent and high area service is maintained.
clueText.nc-c: The trial showed losses fall with pressure, so they are controllable, not an unavoidable growth cost.

tasks.prompt: System water quality strategy case 1: a chloraminated Ontario system sees free ammonia falling and nitrite appearing in Tank A while its other tanks stay clean, and the overall responsible operator must set the response strategy.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional multi tank chloraminated Ontario system. Tank sampling at inlet, outlet and depth points is available, with paired tanks for comparison.

evidence.label: Tank A outlet nitrite reads 0.16 mg/L as N while its inlet reads 0.01 mg/L on the same day.
Free ammonia in Tank A has fallen from 0.44 to 0.13 mg/L over three weeks while total chlorine fell from 1.8 to 0.7 mg/L.
Tank A level cycles only between 82 and 94 percent, giving an estimated water age over 9 days, while Tank B cycles deeply and keeps age under 3 days.
Tank B, fed the same water, shows nitrite below detection and stable residuals.
A trial deep cycling and drawdown of Tank A drops nitrite to 0.03 mg/L and restores total chlorine to 1.4 mg/L within a week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Nitrification is active inside Tank A, driven by long water age from shallow cycling, consuming chloramine and producing nitrite
The treatment plant has started overdosing ammonia for the whole system
A laboratory error is producing false nitrite results for this tank only
A cross connection is feeding untreated water into this tank

inference.explanation: Only in tank nitrification fits nitrite forming across the tank itself, falling free ammonia and total chlorine, long age from shallow cycling, a clean paired tank on the same water, and recovery after deep cycling. A plant dosing change or lab error would affect the paired tank too.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation and guides the strategy?

options.label: Raise the plant chloramine dose for the entire system and wait a month
Take Tank A out of service permanently without further sampling
Trend Tank A nitrite, free ammonia and total chlorine daily during a set deep cycling program, with a water age action level in the nitrification control plan

tasks.prompt: DWQMS internal audit case 1: auditors reviewing chlorine analyser calibration at the Cedar Heights facilities of an Ontario utility find a pattern, and management must decide whether it is an isolated error or a system gap before the management review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario utility operating under the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard, with an approved operational plan, training records and a paired facility for comparison.

evidence.label: Auditors sampled 14 recent records for chlorine analyser calibration at Cedar Heights and 11 of them are missing or incomplete in the same way.
The operational plan requires monthly calibration of continuous chlorine analysers, and the current approved procedure states this clearly.
The procedure was revised 8 months ago, but training and sign off records at Cedar Heights cover only the old version.
A paired facility in the same utility, where the revised procedure was briefed and signed off, shows complete records for the same period.
A 4 week trial at Cedar Heights using the revised procedure with a simple checklist produces complete records for every event.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: One operator made a single isolated recording error
The auditors assessed the records against the wrong procedure version
A systemic implementation gap: the revised procedure was issued but never implemented or trained at Cedar Heights, so the same record failure repeats
An equipment failure prevented the records from being created

inference.explanation: The same gap repeats across most sampled records, the current procedure is clear, the paired facility with training on file is compliant, and a checklist trial produces complete records. A single error, a wrong audit version, or equipment failure cannot explain that pattern.

nextClue.prompt: Which next step best confirms the explanation and guides the strategy?

options.label: Raise a corrective action tracked through management review: brief and sign off the revised procedure, then resample records after 90 days to verify the fix
Discipline the one operator on shift and close the audit finding
Rewrite the procedure again and reissue it without any implementation check

nextClue.explanation: Corrective action with retraining and a dated resampling check tests implementation, which is the gap the audit evidence proves.

clueText.nc-a: Ninety day resampling finds complete records, and management review closes the action with the verification evidence attached.
clueText.nc-b: Most sampled records share the gap, so a single operator error is ruled out by the audit sample itself.
clueText.nc-c: The paired facility complied under the same procedure, so rewriting it again does not address the missing implementation.

tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario cross connection control program with hazard surveys, device test records by premise category and incident investigation reports available.

Two backflow incident investigations in the past year both trace to unprotected or untested devices at premises in this same category.
Device failure rates on tested devices are similar across all categories, near 6 percent.
A focused enforcement trial in one part of the district, with notices and retests, raises category compliance there to 88 percent in one cycle.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residential premises are the main cross connection risk in the system
Test devices are failing mechanically at high rates across all categories
The program risk is concentrated in industrial premises: missing devices and overdue tests there, not a general device or residential problem
The low compliance figure is a database error with no real world gap

options.label: Send a general reminder letter to all customers equally and wait a year
Run a risk based enforcement program starting with every overdue or missing device at high hazard industrial premises, then move down the hazard ranking
Replace all testable devices in the system with new units

nextClue.explanation: Hazard ranked enforcement puts effort where surveys and incidents prove the risk actually sits.
